summary: Preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: The package's preinstall script (node setup.mjs) uses hex-obfuscated identifiers to detect the installer's OS, architecture, and libc (musl vs glibc), downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases into a temp directory, chmods it executable, and uses it to execute a shipped ~727KB heavily obfuscated file, math_init.js, with stdio inherited. math_init.js is marked `@bun @bun-cjs` and uses rotated string arrays, numeric opcode tables, character-set decoder tables, and hex identifier names, rendering it non-reviewable. This behavior runs automatically on `npm install`. The package's declared purpose is a static webpack configuration, which has no legitimate reason to bootstrap an alternate JavaScript runtime and execute an opaque blob at install time. The package.json declares `main: index.js`, but index.js is absent from the tarball — the only install-time effect is the preinstall dropper. This is the canonical alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: an alien runtime is fetched to execute attacker-controlled code that would otherwise be caught by Node-focused scanners, and the payload's content cannot be inspected by installers.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
